Brief facts of the case as per DAR are that on 11.04.2022 at about 02:30, the petitioner Amit Kumar, who was working as a driver with his employer at Shahdara, after finishing his duty, was going to his house at Tila More by his motorcycle bearing no. DL5SAR-4757 and when he reached near Gurudwara, GTB Road, Dilshad Garden, Delhi, an ambulance bearing registration number MP07DA-0821 (hereinafter, "offending vehicle") being driven by its driver at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, came and hit his motorcycle from the front.
As a result, the motorcycle got completely damaged and the petitioner suffered grievous injuries.

sentences.text: Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 11.04.2022 at about 02:30 a.m. near Gurudwara, GTB Road, Dilshad Garden, within the jurisdiction of PS Seemapuri, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. MP07DA-0821, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver? OPP 10.
It is settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal & Ors., (2007) 5 SCC 428.

On this issue, it is seen that the PW1 Amit Kumar, the injured himself, entered into the witness box being eye-witness of the accident and deposed that on 11.04.2022, after finishing duty from Palku Singhal's place, while he was going from Shahdara to his home at Tila More, at around 02:30 a.m. when he reached near Gurudwara, GTB Road by his motorcycle bearing no. DL5SAR-4757,
suddenly an ambulance bearing registration no. MP07DA-0821, being driven at high speed,
negligently and carelessly, came from the wrong side in front of him and hit his bike from the front,
due to which his bike got completely damaged and he received grievous injuries in his leg, hand and head.

PW1 stated that some unknown person got him admitted in GTB Hospital, where his MLC no.
B-684/10/22 was prepared.
PW1 stated that on his statement the criminal case vide FIR no.362/2022, under sections 279/338 IPC was registered at PS Seemapuri, Delhi.

12. It is seen that the aforesaid FIR is part of the DAR before this Tribunal and the registration number of the offending vehicle and that of the motorcycle of the injured are clearly mentioned in the FIR.
Further, the FIR shows that the information about the accident was received at the Police Station on the date of the accident itself vide GD No. 0017A, dated 11.04.2022.
And the mechanical inspection reports of these vehicles, which are part of the DAR, show the accidental damages.

13. sentences.text: With respect to the fact of 7 days delay in lodging the FIR, I may observe that the injured/ PW1 has clarified that, because of pain due to grievous injuries, he was unable to give statement to the Investigating Officer who had visited him in GTB Hospital but later on when he became normal, he went to the Police Station and made a statement to the Investigating Officer and got the FIR lodged.

Besides, the MLC no. B-684/10/22, prepared at GTB Hospital, makes it clear that the petitioner was brought to the hospital immediately after the accident i.e. at 03:20 a.m. on 11.04.2022 in injured condition with the history of RTA (Road Traffic Accident) and the injuries received by him were opined to be grievous in nature.

In view of the above, the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident in question and the same being driven by the respondent no.1 at the time of the accident appears to have not been in dispute.

15. On the aspect of rash and negligent act of the driver/ respondent no.1, this Tribunal observed that though the petitioner (PW1) has stated in his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/X that the offending vehicle i.e. ambulance bearing no.MP07DA-0821 came from the wrong side and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner from front; however, during entire enquiry proceedings,

sentences.text: Also, the Site Plan, which is part of the DAR, also does not indicate that the road on which the accident occurred was a one-way road for plying the traffic only in the direction in which the petitioner was driving his motorcycle.

Thus, as per own version of the petitioner, the accident in question was a head on collusion and the Site Plan makes it clear that it was a single road without any divider and the accident happened in the middle of the road and the petitioner has not been able to prove on record that the offending vehicle was coming on the wrong side at the time of the accident.

Moreover, the mentioning of 'the wrong side'
in the affidavit of evidence Ex.PW1/X in the absence of its mention anywhere in the chargesheet appears to be an improvement.
In the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is held that the petitioner himself was also responsible for the happening of the accident to some extent.

16. In view of the discussion hereinabove, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and the petitioner had also contributed to the happening of the accident to the extent of 25%, which resulted into grievous injuries to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 17. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, enjoins the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on large peripheral field.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury which he might have received in the accident caused by the motor vehicle in a public place, rather he is compensated for the loss, which he suffered as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.

[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 10 SCC 34;
Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45]
and Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

Loss of Income During Treatment 20.

The treatment record of the petitioner Ex.PW1/1 (colly) shows that after the accident on 11.04.2022, the petitioner was taken to GTB Hospital, Delhi, where his MLC was prepared and the petitioner was observed to have suffered a "closed fracture of proximal tibia left (schatzker type-II)"
besides other multiple injuries.
As per Progress Record of the injured/ petitioner prepared at GTB Hospital, despite advice of the doctor, the injured/ petitioner refused his admission in hospital.

Later on, the petitioner got himself hospitalized in IGESIC Hospital, Jhilmil, Delhi, where he remained admitted from 17.05.2022 to 30.05.2022 and during said hospitalization,' ORIF with plating' was done on 25.05.2022.
The treatment record Ex.PW1/1 (colly) shows that his treatment was continued even after he discharged from the hospital.
The prescription dated 25.08.2022 shows that the petitioner was advised three weeks' bed rest.

Considering the nature of the injury and period of treatment, it may be safely assumed that the petitioner must not have been able to do any work for at least five months after his accident and therefore, the petitioner deserves to be compensated for loss of income of said period during treatment.

sentences.text: The petitioner (PW1) has deposed that he was working as Driver with one Palku Singhal at Shahdara, Delhi and was earning Rs.22,000/- to Rs.25,000 per month.

In cross-examination also,
the petitioner (PW1) categorically stated that he was a personal driver.

In support of his deposition with respect to his vocation of being a private driver, the petitioner has placed on record copy of his driving license and proved the same as Ex.PW1/2, which shows that the petitioner was authorized to drive LMV (Light Motor Vehicles).
The driving license Ex.PW1/2 further shows the address of the petitioner as "C-57, Gali no.3, Mukesh Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi-110032".

Thus, the deposition of the petitioner with respect to his vocation of being a private driver is believed by this Tribunal, however,
in the absence of documentary evidence regarding his salary, the income of the petitioner has to be taken at par with minimum wages of skilled workers of Delhi on the date of accident (11.04.2022),
which were Rs.20,019/- per month.

Thus, income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.20,019/- per month and accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,00,095/- (Rs.20,019x5) is granted to the petitioner on account of loss of income of five months during treatment.

sentences.text: 24. In the instant case, PW2 Dr. Amit Srivastava, Associate Professor, GTB Hospital, Delhi produced the original record with respect to issuance of the Disability Certificate to the petitioner.
The Disability Certificate bearing no. 338/14/4/2024, dated 02.04.2024 is on record, as per which the petitioner has suffered 36% permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb.

PW2 (doctor)
deposed that, due to this disability, the petitioner will not be able to walk without support and he will face moderate difficulty in sitting cross-legged and squatting and he will also face mild difficulty in climbing staircase.

In view of this expert opinion of the doctor, it is safely assumed that the petitioner, who was a driver by profession and now as a result of 36% permanent disability in his left lower limb, cannot walk without support, would definitely face difficulties to a considerable extent in performing his work of driving, which requires strength of both legs for operating/ applying accelerator, clutch, brakes, etc., while driving a car.

Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that functional disability in relation to the whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 30% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.
25. Further, the law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal & Ors., (2007) 5 SCC 428.

Considering the nature of the injury and period of treatment, it may be safely assumed that the petitioner must not have been able to do any work for at least five months after his accident and therefore, the petitioner deserves to be compensated for loss of income of said period during treatment.

In view of this expert opinion of the doctor, it is safely assumed that the petitioner, who was a driver by profession and now as a result of 36% permanent disability in his left lower limb, cannot walk without support, would definitely face difficulties to a considerable extent in performing his work of driving, which requires strength of both legs for operating/ applying accelerator, clutch, brakes, etc., while driving a car.
Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of the Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration.
Considering the nature of injury and the period of treatment, an inference can be drawn that the petitioner had to spend a reasonable amount on high and rich protein diet for the purpose of early recovery, especially post surgery, as well as for visiting the hospital/ doctor during further treatment.
The petitioner is also required to be granted attendant charges to compensate the work/ job of his family members, which would definitely have suffered in providing assistance to him in his routine activities during treatment period (Refer : DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Thus, it is clear that due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner during his treatment must have gone through immense pain and suffering, for which Rs.75,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
It is evident that even after completion of treatment, the petitioner suffered 36% permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb, which has been assessed by this Tribunal to be 30%
functional disability in relation to the whole body of the petitioner.
Chargesheet makes it clear that during investigation, driving license (bearing no. DL0819990867234) of the driver/
respondent no.1 was got verified by the Janakpuri Licensing Authority, from where it was reported that "driving license number does not exist"
and accordingly, section 471 IPC was added in the case.
In view of the above, and in the light of section 150(2)(a)(ii) read with section 150(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, this Tribunal is of the view that respondent no.3/ insurance company cannot be directed to pay the compensation and thereafter, it should recover the same from the owner and driver.
Therefore, the respondent no.1, being the driver of the offending vehicle is the principal tortfeasor whereas, respondent no.2, being registered owner would have the vicarious liability.
